ADR, SmartRent Inc., and Trinity Capital Inc. The sources do not provide a definitive answer to any specific question beyond these details.

## FAQ

### What is the Investing.com Earnings Calendar?

The Earnings Calendar is a free tool that tracks earnings report dates for publicly traded companies worldwide. It displays EPS and Revenue forecasts alongside actual results once released, so you can compare analyst expectations with reported outcomes in a single view.

Use our Earnings Calendar to track forecasts for quarterly and annual earnings reports as well as actual outcomes from companies worldwide. Read More [...] An earnings surprise occurs when a company's reported EPS or Revenue differs from the analyst consensus forecast. A positive surprise means the company outperformed expectations, while a negative surprise means it underperformed. The Earnings Calendar displays this as the EPS Surprise % and Revenue Surprise % columns, making it easy to spot which companies beat or missed forecasts at a glance.
